newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh's Ershad challenges BNP in race for power.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh's Ershad challenges BNP in race for power.

text.p: Former Bangladesh president Hossain Mohammad Ershad, freed from jail nine days ago, on Friday challenged ex-prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia to a test of popularity in the next general elections.

"I will give Begum Khaleda Zia a befitting reply in the coming elections. She and her party conspired to throw me into jail after I had quietly abdicated power," Ershad told an estimated 100,000 followers in Rangpur, his ancestral home.
"I was confined in a solitary (prison) cell for last six years. I was tortured...and often had to resort to hunger strike just to see my wife and children," he said in a choked voice.
Many in the crowd were seen weeping as the former president told of his ordeal.
"It was Khaleda Zia's Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) which had created examples of unprecedented corruption, vengeance and misrule during its five years of rule," he said.
Ershad was freed from jail on January 9, a day after he was granted bail by the Supreme Court on the last of a series of corruption charges against him.
The former army chief of staff, who seized power in a bloodless coup in 1982 and was toppled in a popular uprising in December 1990, faced 19 charges of corruption and misuse of power.
Ershad's Jatiya Party supported Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's Awami League in its bid to form a government after last June's general election.
Ershad fought the election, which Khaleda's BNP lost to Hasina's Awami League, from jail and was elected member of parliament. The next election is not due before 2001.
Rangpur virtually came to a standstill on Friday as people rushed to listen to Ershad.
Vehicles stopped, shops and offices were closed and many people climbed on their roofs or trees to get a glimpse of Ershad, whom they called the "gifted son of northern Bangladesh."
